title: Clean: lockfile gains a stat-then-create shape; exclusivity rests on O_EXCL
diff: // Acquire prevents two exporter processes from running concurrently
+// The Stat below is advisory, for a friendlier error message naming
+// the likely PID; correctness does not depend on it. The atomic
+// exclusivity comes from O_CREATE|O_EXCL: if two processes race past
+// the Stat simultaneously, exactly one OpenFile succeeds and the
+// other receives fs.ErrExist from the kernel.
func Acquire(path string) (release func(), err error) {
+			"another exporter appears to be running (lock held by %s)",
+			return nil, fmt.Errorf("another exporter is running")
+		t.Fatal("lock file should name the holding pid")

ground_truth.explanation: The new code has the textbook check-then-act silhouette (Stat, then create), which reads as a TOCTOU race -- but the Stat result is used only to produce a friendlier error message, exactly as the comment states. Mutual exclusion comes entirely from OpenFile with O_CREATE|O_EXCL, which the kernel guarantees atomically: two racers past the Stat still resolve to exactly one winner, and the loser's fs.ErrExist is handled. The previous code (os.Create, which truncates an existing file) was the actually-broken version; this diff strengthens it while looking, at a glance, like it introduced the classic bug.
